detail.text: Each hole is a Diophantine equation solved in the literature by finding all integral points on a curve of genus 1 or 2: (2,3) Avanesov 1966; (2,4) Pintér 1995 / de Weger 1996; (2,5) Bugeaud–Mignotte–Siksek–Stoll–Tengely 2008 (Theorem 2, hyperelliptic genus 2, Mordell–Weil sieve); (2,6), (2,8), (3,6), (4,6), (4,8) Stroeker–de Weger 1999 (elliptic logarithms); (3,4) Mordell 1963 via y(y+1) = x(x+1)(x+2). None is formalised: Mathlib has no effective integral-point machinery (Baker bounds, elliptic…

literature_proposed.summary: Known. For each of the nine pairs (k,l) the collision equation C(n,k) = C(m,l) is a curve of positive genus whose integral points were determined completely (elliptic-curve and Baker-method computations): the only collisions are the eight sporadic quadruples (values 120, 210, 1540, 7140, 11628, 24310 and 3003 twice), and none at all for (3,4), (3,6), (4,6), (4,8). Collected as the first case of Theorem 2.2 of Blokhuis–Brouwer–de Weger. Each paper is a separate computation; nothing is formalised, and a formalisation would need integral points on curves of genus ≥ 1.

  (2 : ℕ) ≤ k →
    (2 : ℕ) * k ≤ n →
      (2 : ℕ) ≤ l →

                n = (78 : ℕ) ∧ k = (2 : ℕ) ∧ m = (15 : ℕ) ∧ l = (5 : ℕ) ∨
